newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end higher, extend gains.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end higher, extend gains.

text.p: Rising bond prices, a stronger franc and record gains on the London and Frankfurt stock markets helped the Paris bourse extend a two-week advance.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 5.82 points, or 0.28 percent, at 2,086.19 after trading in a narrow 14-point range. The CAC-40 futures contract closed up eight points at 2,093.5.
Volume was a heavy 5.01 billion francs.
Tyremaker Michelin rose 2.24 percent ahead of first-half results due out on Tuesday and expected to be good.
The liveliest issue was Eiffage, suspended three times during the session -- twice limit-down and once limit-up.
Eiffage shares slid nearly 20 percent after reporting an 890 million franc loss for the first half, forecasting a similar loss for the full year and suspending the 1996 dividend.
But the stock bounced off its lows after the company predicted a return to profit in 1997. It closed down 23 francs, or just under six percent, at 377.

* Michelin led a rally in the car sector. Analysts have raised their earnings forecasts for Michelin since spring while cutting them for other companies in the sector. One broker said he was expected a profit rise of 20 percent for the tyremaker.

Renault rose 2.35 percent. Traders said the car shares were recovering from a recent hammering. "Some people are betting on the September sales figures," expected to be very strong, a broker said. A year-long state rebate scheme expires at the end of the month.
* General des Eaux buoyed by chairman Jean-Marie Messier's forecast for a "modest" 1996 profit.
* Rhone-Poulenc closed up 1.99 percent after Cholet Dupont analyst raised stock recommendation to buy from accumulate.
* Elf-Aquitaine climbed 0.9 percent to close at 401.60 francs, its highest close since June 1995.
* Strafor-Facom rose 5.47 percent to 424 francs on renewed takeover speculation, fuelled by heavy trading representing four percent of its capital.
* Club Med jumped 4.98 percent to 390 francs after showing an improvement in its 1995/96 third-quarter turnover reflecting the success of its more downmarket Club Aquarius.
* Alcatel Alsthom fell 3.81 percent to 374.10 after confirming it had bid for Thomson. Rival bidder Lagardere closed down 1.05 percent.

The bourse will be watching for two U.S. indicators due to be released on Tuesday -- U.S. industrial production and capacity utilisation for August -- and the French 1997 budget due to be presented on Wednesday.
